A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WildRoad/MaGRoad research and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and four supplementary pages. The references and appendices are identical, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original road-extraction evaluations on WildRoad and three urban benchmarks, component ablations, and qualitative predictions in Sections 5.4–5.6.

after.justification: v3 retains those original benchmark, ablation, runtime, and qualitative results in Tables 2–5 and Figures 4–5.

M1.justification: The path/geometric features, attention, losses, and unified NMS procedure are retained. MaGRoad* is renamed MaGRoad-fast; Section 4.4 expands implementation explanations without establishing a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate WildRoad, City-Scale, SpaceNet, and Global-Scale, including its in-domain and out-of-domain settings. No dataset, task, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains Sat2Graph, SAM-Road, and SAM-Road++; Table 3 retains these methods plus RNGDet++ in each urban comparison. No comparator membership changes.

E3.justification: Data splits, patch and batch sizes, backbone, sampling, optimization, thresholds, and APLS/TOPO metrics are unchanged. The appendix partitioning and inference procedures are also identical.

E4.justification: Both retain the component and node-versus-path ablations in Table 4/Figure 5, pooling-kernel study in Table 5, NMS tradeoff analysis, and scene examples in Figure 4. Section 5.6 is reworded without adding analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests for the benchmark and ablation scores. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: The numerical results and qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, the renamed fast variant still reports F1 82.22, APLS 69.29, and runtime 27.8 minutes in Table 2; its renaming represents no performance change.

T1.justification: Section 4.4 revises the runtime-complexity argument: v1 claims reduced algorithmic complexity, whereas v3 gives O(Nk log N) for the standard implementation and explains implementation overhead. This is a limited revision; Equations (1)–(2) and appendix algorithms remain unchanged, with no new proof.

C1.justification: The claims about WildRoad's novelty, path-centric reasoning, benchmark performance, urban generalization, and roughly 2.5× faster inference are retained. Calling the efficiency contribution 'vertex extraction' specifies the existing contribution rather than changing its scientific scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 changes the speedup explanation from eliminating redundant tree queries and reducing complexity to avoiding array indexing, allocations, and batch writes through scalar operations. The existing completeness-versus-topological-precision tradeoff and applicability discussion remain.

D1.justification: Section 4.4 newly documents scalar neighbor operations and avoidance of intermediate arrays. The abstract's repository target changes from xiaofei-guan/attorch_copy to xiaofei-guan/MaGRoad, although the PDFs cannot establish repository contents or availability. Other implementation settings and appendix details are unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 51 references and related-work discussion are retained. Positioning against node-centric road-extraction methods and existing datasets remains substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites clarify Sections 4.1–4.4 and 5.6 and shorten the conclusion. Terminology changes to MaGRoad-fast and efficient vertex extraction; an author name/contact is corrected, a corresponding-author designation and acknowledgments are added. The overall organization remains intact.

P2.justification: Table 2's variant label and caption change, Figure 3 shifts within page 4, and text/table spacing adjusts around the revisions and acknowledgments. All seven figures and six tables retain their substantive visual content and overall format.

improvement.justification: v3 provides a more concrete explanation of the existing NMS optimization in Section 4.4, replacing broad complexity-reduction language with specific implementation details. Clearer vertex-extraction terminology and localized editing modestly improve technical transparency and readability. The empirical evidence and appendices remain unchanged, so the improvement is limited.
